punchline: Reichheld's book says a large company replaces about half its customers in five years and half its investors in under one.
thirty_sec: Frederick Reichheld argues companies should watch departures as closely as sales. Major firms, he reports, replace about half their customers in five years, half their employees in four and a half, and half their investors in under a year. He treats defection as a measure of failure, argues loyal employees produce loyal customers, and proposes managing to keep the customers likely to stay.
